By integrating this framework into groundwater remediation workflows, we can reduce predictive uncertainty, improve the reliability of long-term forecasts

w:r.w:delText: To move the recalibration framework from concept to practice, a proof-of-principle web application will demonstrate the workflow to DOE-EM and site contractor users. The application will show how new monitoring data trigger uncertainty-based recalibration, and how updated predictions compare with the original model, without requiring users to run the underlying models.

w:r.w:t: The additional FY27 funding will extend the existing pump-and-treat case study to evaluate when recalibration is needed using simulated monitoring observations. The results will be documented in the project report and presented through a simple web demonstration.
We propose a hybrid recalibration framework that integrates physics-based simulations with deep learning models to improve predictive accuracy in groundwater remediation. This dynamic feedback loop
allows more streamlined and efficient adjustments to

Deep Learning Module: Employs advanced deep learning architectures (e.g., U-Net, LSTM networks, diffusion models) capable of capturing complex spatiotemporal groundwater dynamics and delivering rapid predictions.​
Dynamic Recalibration Mechanism: Incorporates an uncertainty quantification module that triggers targeted physics-based simulations when the model encounters high uncertainty or novel conditions.​
Multi-Fidelity Data Integration: Combines diverse data sources, including monitoring data, site characterization data, and simulation outputs, to continually refine and validate the model.​

w:r.w:t: FY27 Recalibration Trigger Evaluation and Demonstration: Using the existing case study, we will compare model predictions with simulated monitoring observations at selected locations to evaluate a recalibration trigger. We will assess whether the trigger identifies declining predictive performance and compare predictions before and after recalibration for both rare and historical conditions. The approach, results, and limitations will be added to the project report. A simple web interface will use prepared datasets and results to present observations, predictions, trigger indicators, and before-and-after comparisons. The interface is for demonstration only and is not intended for regulatory use.
